paragraphs.jp: 七月、りきぞうとやまかわは遠い山村に行った。七夕のおまつりを見に行きたかった。ポチもいっしょに来た。電車は田や川の前をゆっくり走って、小さい駅に着いた。電車が駅に着いてから、二人は地区の小さい駅の待合で少し待った。駅の前には古い民家が少しあって、後ろには高い山林と森林があった。「この山村の地名は何と言うのかな」とりきぞうは言った。やまかわは「だいじょうぶ、村人に聞こう」と明るい顔で言った。
paragraphs.en: In July, Rikizo and Yamakawa went to a far-off mountain village. They wanted to see the Tanabata festival. Pochi came along too. The train ran slowly past rice fields and a river and arrived at a small station. After it arrived, the two waited a little in the waiting area of the small district station. In front of the station stood a few old houses, and behind it were high forested mountains and woodland. They wondered about the place name. Yamakawa said it would be fine and suggested asking a villager.

paragraphs.jp: 二人は村の中心まで歩いた。村には田が多くて、村人が外で仕事をしていた。村の中心まで歩いた時、野犬が前に出た。その野犬はポチを見て、すぐに友だちになった。ポチと野犬は村人の家の前で元気に走った。やまかわはそれを見て、「だいじょうぶだよ」と明るい顔で言った。でも、村人はあまりうれしくない顔をしていた。
paragraphs.en: The two walked to the center of the village. There were many rice fields, and villagers were working outside. As they reached the center, a stray dog stepped out in front of them. It saw Pochi and instantly became friends. Pochi and the stray ran around energetically in front of a villager's house. Watching this, Yamakawa said brightly, "It's fine." But the villagers did not look very happy.

paragraphs.jp: その後、ポチと野犬は村の鳥を見て、元気に走った。鳥は大きい声を出して、空に上がった。村人たちはおどろいて、鳥の後ろを急いで走った。一人の村人が「だれの犬だ」と大きい声で言った。やまかわは「ポチはいい子だよ。だいじょうぶ」と小さい声で言った。でも、ポチと野犬はまだ元気に走っていた。
paragraphs.en: After that, Pochi and the stray spotted the village's chickens and ran around wildly. The birds let out loud cries and flew up into the sky. The startled villagers ran hurriedly after them. One villager shouted, "Whose dog is this?" Yamakawa said quietly, "Pochi is a good boy. It's fine." But Pochi and the stray were still running around.

paragraphs.jp: 村人たちは七夕の紙を家の前に出していた。ポチと野犬はその紙の所まで走って、紙を大きく動かした。きれいな紙が下に動いた。それから、ポチと野犬は村人の食べ物の所に行って、その食べ物を少し食べた。「ああ、私の食べ物が」と村人が言った。やまかわは明るい顔で「ポチはたくさん食べたかったんだね。だいじょうぶ」と言った。りきぞうは「やまかわ、それはだいじょうぶじゃないよ」と思った。
paragraphs.en: The villagers had set out their Tanabata papers in front of their houses. Pochi and the stray ran to the papers and knocked them about. A beautiful paper fell down. Then Pochi and the stray went to a villager's food and ate a little of it. "Oh, my food!" said the villager. Brightly, Yamakawa said, "Pochi just wanted to eat a lot. It's fine." Rikizo thought, "Yamakawa, that is NOT fine."

paragraphs.jp: そこへ村長が来た。村長は町の人があまり好きではなかった。「このおまつりは古い民族のおまつりだ。正道でしなくてはいけない」と村長は言った。村長はりきぞうの洋服を見て、「町の洋服でおまつりの所に入ってはいけない」と言った。「ここでは、犬と村の中を走ってはいけない。村の鳥を見てもいけない」村長は強い声で言った。やまかわは小さい声で「だいじょうぶなのにね」と言った。りきぞうは「すみません」と言った。
paragraphs.en: Just then the village head arrived. He did not much like people from the city. "This is an old festival of our people. It must be done the proper, traditional way," he said. Looking at Rikizo's clothes, he said, "You must not enter the festival grounds in city clothes." "Here you must not run through the village with a dog. You must not even chase the village's birds," he said sternly. Yamakawa muttered quietly, "And yet it'd be fine." Rikizo said, "I'm sorry."

paragraphs.jp: 村長はりきぞうに「町の人でも、村の正道を学ばなくてはいけない」と言った。「七夕の紙に犬の手を入れてはいけない。村人の食べ物を食べてもいけない」と村長は言った。「でも、正しくおまつりを楽しんでもいい」りきぞうは村長の話を聞いて、このおまつりのことをもっと知ろうと思った。
paragraphs.en: The village head said to Rikizo, "Even city people must learn the village's proper ways." "You must not put a dog's paws on the Tanabata papers. You must not eat the villagers' food," he said. "But you may enjoy the festival properly." Hearing the village head's words, Rikizo decided he wanted to know more about this festival.

paragraphs.jp: りきぞうはこのおまつりのことを究明したかった。だから、何人かの村人に話を聞いた。一人の村人の話では、このおまつりは建国の時からあるそうだ。村人には、このおまつりが正月より大切だと聞いた。古い民族の心が、このまつりの中にあるそうだ。「すごいおまつりだ」とりきぞうは思った。りきぞうのその試みで、村のことが少し分かった。りきぞうはもう一度、村長の所に行った。
paragraphs.en: Rikizo wanted to get to the bottom of this festival, so he asked several villagers about it. According to one villager, the festival has existed since the time the nation was founded. He heard that for the villagers this festival matters even more than New Year. The heart of an old people, it is said, lives within this festival. "What an amazing festival," thought Rikizo. Through that effort he came to understand the village a little. He went once more to the village head's place.

paragraphs.jp: 村長はりきぞうの究明の心を見て、少しうれしくなった。村長は「このまつりは、山林と森林の力をもらうまつりだ」と話した。「村人は山の水と田の仕事のために、七夕に空を見たんだ」りきぞうはその話を紙に書いた。「町の人は正月が大切だ。でも、この山村では、七夕がいちばん大切なんだ」と村長は言った。りきぞうは「分かりました」と明るい顔で答えた。
paragraphs.en: The village head saw Rikizo's investigating heart and grew a little glad. He said, "This festival is one for receiving the power of the mountain forests and woods." "The villagers looked at the sky on Tanabata for the mountain's water and the work of the fields." Rikizo wrote that down on paper. "City people value New Year. But in this mountain village, Tanabata matters most," he said. "I understand," Rikizo answered brightly.

paragraphs.jp: おまつりの日になった。村人たちは朝から七夕の紙を家の前に出した。りきぞうとやまかわも紙を正門の前に出した。夕方、二人はおまつりの正門に行った。その時、強風が来て、七夕の紙が大きく動いた。りきぞうは紙を見ながら正門の前を歩いて、道で転んだ。ポチと野犬がすぐに来て、りきぞうの所で元気に走った。「いたい」とりきぞうは言ったが、すぐに立った。
paragraphs.en: The day of the festival came. From morning the villagers set out their Tanabata papers in front of their houses. Rikizo and Yamakawa set out papers in front of the main gate too. In the evening the two went to the festival's main gate. Just then a strong wind blew and the Tanabata papers swayed greatly. Watching the papers as he walked in front of the gate, Rikizo tripped on the road. Pochi and the stray came right over and ran around where Rikizo was. "Ow," said Rikizo, but he stood right back up.

paragraphs.jp: おまつりの夜、村は明るくなった。村人も町の人も、みんないっしょにおまつりを楽しんだ。ポチと野犬は、もう村の中を元気に走ってもよかった。村長も明るい顔で、子どもたちといっしょにまつりを見ていた。やまかわも道で転んだが、すぐに明るい顔で立った。この山村は、春夏秋冬、いつもきれいなのだろう。今日のことが、りきぞうの心に去来した。「この山村に来てよかった」とりきぞうは思った。
paragraphs.en: On the night of the festival, the village grew bright. Villagers and city folk alike enjoyed the festival all together. Pochi and the stray were now even allowed to run around the village. The village head, too, watched with a cheerful face beside the children. Yamakawa also tripped on the road, but he popped right back up with a bright face. This mountain village must be lovely all year round, through every season. The day's events came and went in Rikizo's heart. "I'm glad I came to this mountain village," thought Rikizo.

paragraphs.jp: おまつりの後、村長がりきぞうたちの所に来た。村長は明るい顔で、「あの犬たちは、この山村のおまつりを明るくしたな」と言った。「町の人でも、また来てもいい。来年もこの山村に来てもいいよ」りきぞうはとてもうれしくなった。「ありがとうございます。来年も七夕に来ます」と言った。やまかわは明るい顔で「だいじょうぶでしたね」と言った。ポチと野犬も、村長の前で元気に走った。
paragraphs.en: After the festival, the village head came over to Rikizo and the others. With a cheerful face he said, "Those dogs really brightened up this mountain village's festival." "Even city folk may come again. You may come to this mountain village next year too." Rikizo was overjoyed. "Thank you very much. We'll come for Tanabata next year too," he said. With a bright face, Yamakawa said, "It was fine, see?" Pochi and the stray, too, ran happily in front of the village head.
